entities.summary: Gilles Deschamps was a teacher and bishop of Coutances, a key figure in the medieval Catholic Church, who played a pivotal role in shaping the theological and ecclesiastical landscape of 15th-century France. Created cardinal by Antipope John XXIII on 6 July 1411, Deschamps was a significant figure in the theological debates of his time, particularly in the context of the conciliar movement. His influence can be seen in the works of Jean Gerson, who studied under both Deschamps and Pierre d'Ailly, and in the development of the French tradition of scholastic theology. Despite his important role in the Catholic Church, Deschamps' legacy is often overshadowed by that of his contemporaries, and he remains a relatively lesser-known figure in the annals of medieval history. Deschamps' story is one of spiritual guidance, intellectual curiosity, and the complexities of ecclesiastical politics.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Gilles Deschamps played a significant role in shaping the theological and ecclesiastical landscape of 15th-century France, particularly through his connection to the conciliar movement and his influence on the development of French scholastic theology.
